sections_target.text: This document sets out the steps for the semi-annual inspection of the automatic fire extinguishing system in the turbine hall.

There is a complete fire-fighting system using CO2, with 32 cylinders distributed over two parts, one for the control cabinets and auxiliaries and the other for the turbine itself; each part consists of 16 cylinders.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Hani El-Oqda, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, approved by Eng. Mohamed El-Sherif, General Manager of Instruments, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Magid Sawan, Head of Nubaria Power Station Sector.

It was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and the document was approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the company's coordinator for the Maintenance Procedures Information System, and certified by Eng. Mohamed Naguib Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.

rows: Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; those carrying out the maintenance must hold an Occupational Safety and Health category card.
Fence off the place to define the work area and put up warning signs.
Follow the occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment and wear personal protective equipment (safety helmet, safety shoes, overalls, gloves, ...).
Complete tool bag
Cleaning fluids
Make sure the number of cylinders in the system is complete: (32) cylinders
Check the response of the suspension weights to movement.

Inspect the mechanical weights placed on the distributor to ensure the system is ready and stable and will operate when needed, as there are four common cylinders: if the weight of any one of them drops, the remaining cylinders are discharged.
Make sure the electrical connections are sound.
Make sure all the arms are engaged with the cylinder valves.
Make sure the fire system monitoring panel is working properly
Make sure the pressure indicator on the fire line is working properly
Make sure the fire sensors are sound
Make sure the fire system lines are sound
Make sure the release cabinet is prepared in accordance with the operating instructions.
Test the solenoid valve and make sure it is clean and working
Make sure the CO2 discharge nozzles are working properly and maintain them if necessary

Introduction
This document sets out the steps for the semi-annual inspection of the automatic fire extinguishing system in the turbine hall.
There is a complete fire-fighting system using CO2, with 32 cylinders distributed over two parts, one for the control cabinets and auxiliaries and the other for the turbine itself; each part consists of 16 cylinders.
The first draft was prepared by Eng. Ahmed Mohamed El-Mohtady Qamra, tested by Eng. Hani El-Oqda, and reviewed by
Eng. El-Said Shaaban Abdel Qader, approved by Eng. Mohamed El-Sherif, General Manager of Instruments, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Abdel Magid Sawan, Head of Nubaria Power Station Sector.
It was reviewed by Chemist Ibrahim Youssef Youssef, Occupational Safety and Health Inspector in the Inspection Sector, and the document was approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Galil, General Manager of Inspection and Quality Control at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company and the company's coordinator for the Maintenance Procedures Information System, and certified by Eng. Mohamed Naguib Abdel Hay, Head of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector at the Middle Delta Electricity Production Company.
Safety Precautions
Issue an approved work order from the competent authority; those carrying out the maintenance must hold an Occupational Safety and Health category card. | 
Fence off the place to define the work area and put up warning signs. | 
Follow the occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment and wear personal protective equipment (safety helmet, safety shoes, overalls, gloves, ...). |

Make sure the release cabinet is prepared in accordance with the operating instructions. | 10.
Test the solenoid valve and make sure it is clean and working | 11.
Make sure the CO2 discharge nozzles are working properly and maintain them if necessary | 12.
